title: Tenant-aware cursor pagination and shard-aware caching for dashboard query API
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Dashboard query API (GET /v1/console/metrics) is experiencing long tail latency and excessive DB CPU on tenants with high-cardinality events. Current offset-based pagination causes deep OFFSET scans and repeated identical subqueries for large result sets; current cache layer stores full query fingerprints but is ineffective for cursor-driven UIs because clients re-request overlapping windows and multi-tenant workload skews cache hit-rate.

Goal: Implement a tenant-aware cursor pagination scheme (stable cursor tokens referencing shard + time-slice) combined with shard-aware result caching and lightweight pre-aggregation to reduce DB CPU, lower 95/99th percentile latencies, and improve cache hit rates for paginated dashboard queries. This ticket covers the backend API contract, query planner hints, index adjustments, Redis caching keys, and rollout plan.

Current metrics:
- 95p latency: 1.4s for heavy tenants (window=30d, group_by=endpoint)
- DB CPU attributed to dashboard queries: ~22% during peak hours
- Cache hit rate for dashboard queries: ~12% overall, <5% for top 10 high-cardinality tenants

Non-goals: Rewrite telemetry pipeline or change retention; not touching OLAP storage format (we'll operate on current analytics tables and pre-agg materialized view layer as needed).

Design summary:
1) Cursor model: issue stable opaque cursor token: base64(JSON) with {tenant_id, shard_id, time_bucket_start, sort_key_last, version}. Cursor semantics are forward-only and map to a pre-filtered time-slice + index range; no OFFSET.
2) Shard-aware routing: use existing tenant -> analytics shard mapping (service: analytics-shard-mapper) to route queries and select the correct DB replica. Add a routing hint to the SQL layer so queries avoid cross-shard scans.
3) Indexing: add composite indexes for common predicates: (tenant_id, time_bucket, group_key, sort_key) and explicit partial indexes for extremely high-cardinality tenants (pattern: tenant_id IN (..)). Work with infra to schedule index creation during low-traffic windows.
4) Query rewrite: convert client requests to windowed queries limited by time_bucket + sort_key > cursor_last using LIMIT page_size + 1 to detect next cursor. Use optimizer hints to prefer index scan.
5) Caching: introduce two-layer cache: a) short-lived pre-aggregation cache keyed by (tenant_id, time_bucket, group_by_hash, rollup_level) with TTL 60s; b) per-tenant cursor-result cache keyed by (tenant_id, cursor_token) with TTL 30s and size cap per-tenant. Cache located in Redis cluster with shard awareness to avoid cross-tenant cache eviction storms.
6) Telemetry and safety: emit metrics for cursor hops, cache hit/miss per-tenant, tail-latency per-request, and fallback path counts. Provide feature-flag and canary routing that allows 10% of tenants to use new cursor flow initially.

API compatibility: Old offset-based queries will remain supported for 90 days. New clients may pass query_param pagination=cursor to opt-in. The server will return a next_cursor in the same object shape used for subsequent requests. Backwards compatibility document: https://confluence.redwood.ai/console/pagination-migration

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field below.

Engineering trade-offs considered:
- Cursor tokens increase server-side complexity and require careful invalidation for data updates; accepted because analytics data is append-only for most pipelines and time-bounded dashboards tolerate eventual consistency.
- Per-tenant cache caps increase operational memory bookkeeping; we avoid global caching that allowed noisy neighbors to evict useful entries.
- Creating partial indexes for top tenants reduces query cost for few tenants but increases write amplification; recommended only for top ~5 tenants by traffic---we will automate index recommendations via a follow-up job.
acceptance_criteria: API returns next_cursor and no OFFSET in query plan for cursor-enabled requests
95th/99th p95/p99 latency reduced by >=25% for canary tenants compared to baseline
DB CPU attributed to dashboard queries drops by at least 15% during canary window
Cache hit-rate for paginated dashboard queries improves to >=40% for canary tenants
No increase in error rate (>0.1%) or incorrect pagination results across a 48-hour canary
Rollout plan and rollback steps documented with runbook and feature flags
implementation_steps: spec: finalize token format and publish to Confluence (doc link) - owner: Tomás
backend: add cursor parameter parsing and validation; generate next_cursor - owner: Tomás
sql: add optimizer hints and LIMIT-based rewrites; add new SQL templates - owner: Maria Petrov
infra: schedule index creation windows and prepare migration scripts - owner: Ops team
cache: implement shard-aware Redis keying and per-tenant caps - owner: Ravi Iyer
telemetry: dashboard and alerting for cursor flow metrics - owner: Priya Nair
tests: unit + integration tests that validate pagination correctness and concurrency behavior - owner: QA
canary: enable feature-flag for 10% tenants; run 72-hour canary and evaluate metrics - owner: SRE/Oncall
risks_and_mitigation: Stale cursors after materialized view refreshes: mitigate by embedding time_bucket and version in cursor; if version mismatch return 410 and provide resync hint
Cache thrash from noisy tenants: mitigate via per-tenant caps and LRU eviction; limit concurrent cached cursors per tenant
Index creation impacts writes: schedule during low traffic and stagger indexes; monitor replication lag
Client implementations mis-handle opaque token: include detailed spec and example SDK helper in SDK repo
metrics_and_dashboards: DD:dashboards/console/dashboard-pagination-overview - overview of latency, DB CPU, cache hit-rate
DD:dashboards/console/cursor-flow-by-tenant - per-tenant cursor hops and miss rates
Alerts: >5% error rate for cursor requests over 10m -> pager
